passages.title: Dialogue 1: A camping trip
passages.text:
Man: So how was the camping trip? You weren't very keen before you went.
Woman: I know! I thought I'd hate sleeping in a tent, and when it rained on the first night I nearly came home. But honestly, it turned out to be one of the best holidays I've ever had. The campsite was lovely, it cost almost nothing, and I didn't miss my phone at all.
Man: So you'd go again?
Woman: Definitely.

passages.title: Dialogue 2: Planning a trip to Edinburgh
passages.text:
Woman: If we drive to Edinburgh, we can stop wherever we like on the way.
Man: True, but it's eight hours at the wheel, and parking in the city centre is a nightmare.
Woman: Mm, fair point. And on the train we could read or sleep.
Man: Exactly. And it's not much more expensive if we book now.
Woman: Right, let's do that. But I'm not getting up at five to catch the first one!
Man: No, the one at ten is fine. What about the hotel?
Woman: I'd still prefer somewhere outside the centre. It's quieter.
Man: Hmm. We can sort that out later.

passages.title: Dialogue 3: A hotel in Lisbon
passages.text:
Woman: How was the hotel in Lisbon?
Man: The rooms were a bit small, and I'd read online that the street outside was noisy, but actually we didn't hear a thing at night. What I really liked was that it was right in the old town, so we could walk everywhere. The breakfast was great too, lots of fresh fruit and local cakes.
Woman: Sounds perfect.

passages.title: Dialogue 4: Going back to Spain
passages.text:
Man: You're off to Spain again? Visiting your cousins?
Woman: Not this time. They're coming over here in the summer. I've booked a two-week course in Seville. My Spanish is getting really rusty, and I'll need it for my new job.
Man: Lucky you. Seville's near the coast, isn't it?
Woman: Not that near, and anyway I doubt I'll have time for the beach. There are classes every morning and homework every evening!

passages.title: Dialogue 5: City breaks
passages.text:
Woman: I'm thinking of doing a weekend in Paris. Have you ever done a city break?
Man: A couple. They're not as expensive as people think, if you book early. And I don't mind all the walking, actually. My problem is that by the time you've found your way around, it's time to go home. I'd rather go somewhere for a whole week and really get to know the place.

passages.title: Dialogue 6: A phone call to an airline
passages.text:
Man: Good morning, Skyway Airlines. Is this about the delays on today's flights?
Woman: No, no, my flight isn't until next week. I'm booked to Rome on the fourteenth, reference AB172. My sister's wedding has been moved, so I won't need to be there until the sixteenth. Could you put me on a flight that day instead? I'm happy to pay the difference. Oh, and I've already read the information about hand luggage, so I don't need to ask about that.
Man: Let me see what I can do.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about a camping trip. What does the woman say about it?
options: a) It cost more than she had planned.
b) The bad weather spoilt it.
c) It was better than she had expected.
questions.explanation: She wasn't keen before she went and 'thought I'd hate sleeping in a tent', but it 'turned out to be one of the best holidays I've ever had'. It rained only on the first night and did not spoil the trip, and she says it 'cost almost nothing'.

questions.question: You will hear two friends planning a trip to Edinburgh. What do they agree about?
options: a) They should go by train.
b) They should leave very early in the morning.
c) They should stay outside the city centre.
questions.explanation: After the man points out the problems with driving, the woman says 'on the train we could read or sleep' and 'Right, let's do that'. She refuses to catch the first train at five, and they do not agree about the hotel: the man says 'We can sort that out later'.

questions.question: You will hear a man talking about a hotel he stayed in. What did he like most about it?
options: a) Its position in the town
b) How quiet it was at night
c) The size of the rooms
questions.explanation: He says 'What I really liked was that it was right in the old town, so we could walk everywhere'. The rooms were 'a bit small', and although it was quiet at night, he mentions this only because he had expected noise; it is not what he liked most.

questions.question: You will hear a woman talking about a trip to Spain. Why is she going?
options: a) To spend time on the beach
c) To visit members of her family
questions.explanation: She has booked a course because 'My Spanish is getting really rusty, and I'll need it for my new job'. Her cousins are coming to visit her instead, and she doubts she will have time for the beach.

questions.question: You will hear two friends talking about city breaks. What is the man's opinion of them?
questions.explanation: His problem is that 'by the time you've found your way around, it's time to go home', and he would rather go 'for a whole week'. He says they are 'not as expensive as people think' and that he doesn't mind all the walking.

questions.question: You will hear a woman phoning an airline. Why is she calling?
options: a) To complain about a delay
b) To change the date of her flight
c) To ask what she can take on the plane
questions.explanation: She asks 'Could you put me on a flight that day instead?' because she now needs to travel on the sixteenth, not the fourteenth. She says her call is not about today's delays, and she has already read the information about hand luggage.
